text: The type of hybridisation and magnetic property of the complex [MnCl$_{6}$]$^{3-}$, respectively, are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $[\mathrm{MnCl}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ manganese is in the $+3$ state: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{4}$.

$\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is a weak-field ligand, so the four 3d electrons stay unpaired in four separate 3d orbitals and two vacant inner 3d orbitals are not available. The six ligand electron pairs therefore occupy the 4s, three 4p and two 4d orbitals, giving outer-orbital $sp^{3}d^{2}$ hybridisation.


[IMG]

With 4 unpaired electrons the complex is paramagnetic ($μ=\sqrt{24}=4.90\text{BM}$).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text:
The number of geometrical isomers found in the metal 
complexes [PtCl$_{2}(NH_{3})_{2}$], [$Ni(CO)_{4}$], [$Ru(H_{2}O)_{3}Cl_{3}$] and [CoCl$_{2}(NH_{3})_{4}$]$^{+}$ respectively, are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{PtCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{2}]$ is square planar of type $\mathrm{MA}{}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{2}$: cis and trans forms, so 2 geometrical isomers.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$ is tetrahedral with four identical ligands; all positions of a tetrahedron are adjacent to one another, so it shows no geometrical isomerism: 0.

$[\mathrm{Ru}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}]$ is octahedral of type $\mathrm{MA}{}_{3}\mathrm{B}{}_{3}$: facial and meridional forms, so 2.

$[\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}]^{+}$ is octahedral of type $\mathrm{MA}{}_{4}\mathrm{B}{}_{2}$: cis and trans forms, so 2.

The numbers are 2, 0, 2, 2.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

[IMG]

Consider the above reaction and identify the Product P :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Cyclohexylmethanol is protonated by $\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{PO}{}_{4}$ and loses water on heating (E1). As water leaves, a 1,2-hydride shift from the ring carbon gives the tertiary 1-methylcyclohexyl cation instead of a primary carbocation.

Loss of a ring proton from this cation gives the more substituted (Saytzeff) alkene, 1-methylcyclohexene, as the major product A.

Hydroboration–oxidation adds H and OH syn and anti-Markovnikov: OH goes to the less substituted alkene carbon (C-2) and H to the methyl-bearing carbon (C-1).

So P is 2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol (the trans isomer), the structure in option (D). The minor exocyclic alkene, methylenecyclohexane, would give back cyclohexylmethanol, option (A).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text:
The density of NaOH solution is $1.2 g cm^{-3}$. The molality of this solution is $_____________ m. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer)

[Use : Atomic mass : Na : 23.0 u, O : 16.0 u, H : 1.0 u, Density of $H_{2}O$ : $1.0 g cm^{-3}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Consider 1 litre solution

mass of solution = (1.2 $\times$ 1000)g = 1200 gm

Neglecting volume of NaOH

Mass of water = 1000 gm

$\Rightarrow$ Mass of NaOH = (1200 $-$ 1000)gm = 200 gm

$\Rightarrow$ Moles of NaOH = $\frac{200g}{40g/mol}=5$ mol

$\Rightarrow$ molality = $\frac{5mol}{1kg}=5$ m

text: The conductivity of a weak acid HA of concentration 0.001 mol $L^{-1}$ is 2.0 $\times$ $10^{-5} S cm^{-1}$. If $\Lambda _{m}^{o}(HA) = 190 S cm^{2}$ mol$^{-1}$, the ionization constant $(K_{a})$ of HA is equal to $______________$ $\times$ $10^{-6}. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Lambda m=1000\times \frac{κ}{M}$

$=1000\times \frac{2\times 10^{-5}}{0.001}=20$ $S cm^{2}$ mol$^{-1}$

$\Rightarrow α=\frac{\Lambda m}{\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }}=\frac{20}{190}=\left (\frac{2}{19}\right )$

HA $⇌$ $H^{+} + A^{-}$

$0.001(1-α)0.001α0.001α$

$\Rightarrow k_{a}=0.001\left (\frac{α^{2}}{1-α}\right )=\frac{0.001\times \left (\frac{2}{19}\right )^{2}}{1-\left (\frac{2}{19}\right )}$

$=12.3\times 10^{-6}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: The number of geometrical isomers possible in triamminetrinitrocobalt (III) is X and in trioxalatochromate (III) is Y. Then the value of X + Y is $_______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) is $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{3}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}){}_{3}]$, an octahedral $\mathrm{Ma}_{3}\mathrm{b}_{3}$ complex. The three $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ groups can lie on one face (fac) or along one meridian (mer), so X = 2. Bonding of the ambidentate $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ through N or O gives linkage isomers, not geometrical isomers.

Trioxalatochromate(III) is $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$, an $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{AA})_{3}$ complex. With three identical symmetrical bidentate ligands only one geometrical arrangement exists; the complex shows only optical isomerism (d and l forms), so Y = 0.


[IMG]

$X+Y=2+0=2$

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text:
For water at 100${}^{\circ }$ C and 1 bar,

$\Delta_{vap}$ H $-$ $\Delta_{vap}$ $U = _____________$ $\times$ $10^{2} J$ mol$^{-1}. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer)

[Use : R = 8.31 J mol$^{-1} K^{-1}$]

[Assume volume of $H_{2}O(l)$ is much smaller than volume of $H_{2}O(g)$. Assume $H_{2}O(g)$ treated as an ideal gas]

For 1 mole waters;

$\Delta n_{g} = 1$

$\therefore$ $\Delta n_{g}RT = 1$ mol $\times$ 8.31 J/mol-k $\times$ 373 K

= 3099.63 J $\cong$ 31 $\times$ $10^{2} J$
